params.body:
## What Shane saw

On a phone (390 px), the Schade step showed the exploded-view drawing with eighteen numbered buttons. "Extra schade" overlapped button 16, button 1 was half off the right edge, and a bare number said nothing about which panel it was. His words: "schade afbeelding niet echt bruikbaar op mobiel". And with a part's form open, scrolling inside it scrolled the sheet underneath: "als ik op mobiel scroll op de modal scrolt het onderliggend".

## 1. On a phone the damage step is a list of parts by name

Under 768 px the drawing gives way to a list: one thumb-high row per part, named from `Enumeration::damageParts()` in the dealer's language, in the order of the drawing, place 18 "Extra schade" last. A damaged row carries the same amber its button carries; the open one the same blue. Above 768 px the drawing is exactly what it was.

**Nothing is duplicated.** A row is another way to press `button_<n>`: the delegated click handler calls `button.click()`, so `showTextArea`, the backdrop, `addDamage` and `recolorDamageButtons` stay the only path. The row reads its state (damaged, open) from its button through a MutationObserver on the drawing, so there is no second place that knows what is damaged. The PHP judgement "damaged = a remark or a photo" (R S1-6.17) is computed once per position and shared by button and row.

**Why 767 px.** It is the breakpoint the sheet already uses for its header sheets and for the damage photo tiles (28 `@media (max-width: 767px)` blocks in refresh.css), and it is where the drawing stops working: the layout is single-column under 992 px with the drawing capped at 560 px, so down to 768 px the drawing keeps its full 560 px and its buttons stay 95 px apart; under that the drawing shrinks with the viewport and the buttons start touching. 480 px (the stepper grid) is too late: at 450 px the pairs 14/8, 15/3, 16/12, 17/4 already overlap.

**Why not a scaled drawing.** The drawing already is one: `_create_vehicle.scss` positions every button in percentages (`#button_1 { top: 46%; left: 94% }`), so what Shane photographed is the scaled drawing. The failure is a size, not a positioning bug: at 362 px the drawing is 252 px high and the buttons are still 40 px, so four pairs overlap (14 on 8, 15 on 3, 16 on 12, 17 on 4) and 1 hangs over the edge. Shrinking the buttons would make it worse: eighteen 44 pt targets need 38% of a 362 x 252 box, and the panels in the drawing are smaller than the buttons already. A thumb cannot hit it regardless of positioning, which was the expectation, confirmed.

## 2. An open dialog scrolls itself, never the page behind it

The damage form had no lock, and the check the coordinator asked for found the same hole in both shared layers:

- `modal.js` puts `modal-open` on the body, which the theme styles as `overflow: hidden`. iOS Safari ignores that for touch, so the offer/order/terms modals scroll the page too.
- The Livewire/Alpine overlays (`ui-modal-overlay`: in-option, sold, average price) put nothing on the body at all.

So it is fixed once, in `resources/js/dialog-lock.js`, and not called by any dialog: while any displayed element declares itself modal (`aria-modal="true"`) the document is locked, and when the last one is gone it is released. modal.js already sets `aria-modal` on show and removes it on hide; the `ui-modal-dialog`s carry it; the damage form now declares it. That is why no close path has to remember the release (the X, the backdrop, Escape, a Livewire re-render that drops the overlay, the observer that closes the damage form after a save) and a lock cannot outlive its dialog. The lock is the iOS-proof shape: `html.ui-scroll-locked body { position: fixed; width: 100% }` with the scroll offset as a negative `top`, restored on release. Each dialog is its own scroll container with `overscroll-behavior: contain`; on a phone the damage form fills the screen.

**Why the damage overlay bypassed the shared layer.** It is not a modal at all: `showTextArea` toggles `d-none` on one of eighteen in-page divs and CSS renders the visible one fixed and centred, with its own backdrop. It predates modal.js and never went through `.modal`/`modal-open`. It now shares the lock by declaring `aria-modal`, which is the one thing the three systems have in common.

**Measured at 390 px** (driven in the browser, not screenshots): sheet scrolled to 442 px; open part 12 from the list: body `position: fixed; top: -442px`, `document.scrollingElement.scrollHeight` 600 = `innerHeight` 600 (nothing left to scroll), `window.scrollTo(0, 800)` and `scrollBy(0, 300)` leave `scrollY` at 0; close with the X: lock gone, `scrollY` 442. Same via Escape and via the backdrop. Terms modal (modal.js): locked while open. Average-price overlay (Livewire, prices tab): scrolled 744.5 px, open: `top: -744.5px`, `scrollY` 0 after `scrollTo(0, 1500)`; closed: 744.5. The offer modal itself could not be opened on the local box (its route returned a full page for this dealer), so the shared layer is covered by the terms modal that goes through the same `_show`/`_hide`.

## Docs and tests

- Rules R S1-6.27 (the phone list) and R S1-6.28 (a dialog scrolls itself) in `11-s1-wagen-invoeren-en-beheren.md`, both tagged from `DamageTabTest`.
- Finding as its own file: `docs/bedrijfsregels/bevindingen/2026-09-15-schade-op-telefoon.md` (new procedure, no X number).
- `DamageTabTest`: the sheet renders the drawing and eighteen named rows, in order, each pointing at an existing button, the damaged one marked and only that one; the rows are bound in a script and press their button; the swap is CSS on 767 px. And: every damage form declares itself modal, the lock exists once and is loaded once, the body is fixed while locked, and each of the three dialog systems has `overscroll-behavior: contain`.
- `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter='Damage|VehicleForm|OwnStock|StylesheetSyntax|AlpineExpression|HandlerWiring|RulesCoverage'`: OK (70 tests, 1050 assertions) on the rebased tree.
params.title: The damage drawing was unusable on a phone, and its dialog scrolled the page behind it
